answer: One identity is tied to one buried tank, because a state environmental agency registers an underground storage tank only after a licensed installation, leak-detection equipment, and financial assurance for cleanup. Three established peers check the tank registration, the installer's certificate, the leak-detection test results, and a fresh signature before the agent can answer. Each fake pays $50,000 to $100,000 for its own hollow steel tank, so a garden of impostors costs $50 million before a single answer, like a thread that only ties one tank to one identity at a time.
